name: WhiteFiber, Inc. (Cayman Islands exempted company; formerly White Fiber, Inc.; incorporated as Celer, Inc.)
headquarters: New York, NY, USA (31 Hudson Yards, Floor 11); Canadian data-centre subsidiary Enovum in Montreal, Quebec

ownership.notes: Listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market on 7 Aug 2025 (IPO at US$17.00; US$183.3M gross with the over-allotment). Bit Digital, Inc. (Nasdaq: BTBT) contributed the business on 6 Aug 2025 for 27,043,749 shares and still holds 27,043,750: 74.3% at the IPO, 70.5% at 31 Dec 2025, 69.6% on 12 Aug 2026 and approximately 59.9% after WhiteFiber issued about 6.3 million shares in the 21 Aug 2026 convertible-note exchange (Schedule 13D/A, 25 Aug 2026, on about 45.1 million shares outstanding). WhiteFiber is a 'controlled company' under Nasdaq rules and says it does not currently rely on the exemptions. Bit Digital says it will not sell WhiteFiber shares in 2026 and signed a 60-day lock-up from 18 Aug 2026. No spin-off distribution has been announced. Sam Tabar is chief executive of both companies.

summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: WhiteFiber is a Bit Digital-controlled, Nasdaq-listed operator of two businesses: a GPU cloud that SemiAnalysis rates 'Underperforming', and a retrofit data-centre landlord (Enovum) whose one big lease, 40 MW IT to Nscale at NC-1 in Madison, North Carolina for about US$865 million over ten years, is 93% of its US$1.0 billion of remaining performance obligations. It signs for its own sites: it bought NC-1 (US$45 million base) and MTL-3, is buying two more North Carolina buildings for US$60 million, holds the Duke Energy Carolinas service agreement for NC-1 through Enovum NC-1 Bidco, LLC, and disclosed on 14 May 2026 'a recently identified supply-chain-related issue affecting certain medium-voltage switchgear components' that pushed Nscale's April and May 2026 ready-for-service dates into the third quarter. BACKGROUND: Bit Digital formed the AI business in October 2023, bought Enovum Data Centers (Montreal) in October 2024, launched the WhiteFiber brand in February 2025 and floated it in August 2025. Sites: MTL-1 (4 MW gross, leased), MTL-2 (5 MW, owned, restarted in Q3 2026), MTL-3 (7 MW gross, Cerebras as sole tenant, bought in May 2026), NC-1 (54 gross MW delivered by Duke, a 99 MW target by May 2029), and NC-2/NC-3 in Yadkin County (60 to about 200 MW, closing Q4 2026). Cloud capacity is leased in Iceland, Atlanta, Paris and, from Q4 2026, Sydney. FY2025 revenue was US$79.2 million (cloud US$68.8 million) with a US$24.7 million net loss; H1 2026 revenue was US$50.8 million. Financed by two convertible issues (US$230 million due 2031, US$310 million due 2032), a related-party US$100 million delayed-draw loan from Bit Digital for NC-1, RBC and Landsbankinn facilities, and a proposed NC-1 project financing in exclusivity as of August 2026. Per company filings unless stated; the 10-K, 10-Qs, prospectus and 8-Ks were read on EDGAR, which was reachable from this session.
ecosystemRole: We assess WhiteFiber as the corpus's clearest small-cap case of a neocloud that is also a data-centre owner, and the landlord through which a larger neocloud (Nscale) reaches Duke Energy. Basis: the Duke Energy Carolinas capacity letter (16 May 2025) and Unifi's assigned electric service agreement (4 Aug 2025) are held by WhiteFiber's subsidiary, Enovum NC-1 Bidco, LLC, not by Nscale; Duke owns the 'Extra Facilities (including overhead lines, substations, transformers, breakers, and metering equipment)' under that agreement, while WhiteFiber buys what sits behind the meter: 'power distribution equipment, generators, and cooling systems' and 'power distribution units' (10-K). Its retrofit model targets US$8 to 10 million per gross MW and about six months per build. For a power-equipment seller the buying authority is real but modest in size: one 40 MW IT phase built, 54 gross MW delivered, an unnamed general contractor and unnamed switchgear suppliers, natural-gas fuel cells intended behind the meter 'by partnering with third-party energy providers', and no SST, 800 VDC or battery project on the record. The named opening is the MV switchgear category, where a supply issue delayed the company's largest contract.

productsAndServices.name: WhiteFiber Cloud — GPU cloud services (the 'Cloud services' segment)
productsAndServices.description: Bare-metal, containerised and virtualised NVIDIA GPU capacity sold as reserved instances, managed private cloud and bespoke large deployments, on hardware WhiteFiber owns or, under a 'capital-light managed-services offering', that the customer funds and WhiteFiber operates. The catalogue lists HGX GB300, HGX B300, HGX H100 and VR200, with a '3.2 Tb/s Infiniband and RoCE GPU Fabric', 'Up to 800 Gb/s Ethernet' and a claimed 'AVERAGE 99.95% Uptime'. The 10-K calls the company 'among the first service providers to offer H200, B200, and GB200 servers' and lists its channels: an NVIDIA Preferred Partner, a Supermicro authorised partner, a Dell CSP (through Advania), an HPE partnership and a QCT relationship. The first GB200 NVL72 shipment arrived from Quanta in April 2025. Capacity sits in leased space: Blönduós, Iceland (6 MW gross, 5.5 MW IT contracted, hydro), Atlanta (two leases from February 2026), third-party space in the Paris region and, from Q4 2026, a Sydney lease.
highlights: Cloud revenue: US$45.7M (FY2024), US$68.8M (FY2025), US$16.8M (Q1 2026), US$23.8M (Q2 2026); the initial customer that was 70.7% of FY2025 revenue was terminated in Q2 2026 under an agreement preserving US$12.5M of receivables, and Bit Digital's 10-Q says WhiteFiber's largest customer was about 63% of H1 2026 revenue

Contracts disclosed since May 2026 (company figures, none confirmed by the customer): Hyperbolic/Modal Labs (2 years, ~US$17M, H200); an investment-grade technology customer in the Paris region (5 years, >US$160M TCV, RFS targeted 30 Sep 2026); Prime Intellect (576 VR200 in Canada, 3 years, ~US$108M, service Q2 2027); BaseTen (1,392 B300, 36 months, ~US$165.2M, revenue from Nov 2026); an existing Iceland customer (576 B300, 5 years, ~US$87.5M, Dec 2026); Krambu (100 MW of exclusive liquid-cooled capacity from 2027, Q2 2026 call). The September 2026 deck claims '>$550M recent cloud TCV', '7,500+ NVIDIA GPUs contracted' and '20+ customers'

Independent rating: SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX 2.0 (6 Nov 2025) placed WhiteFiber in 'Not Recommended – Underperforming' for a non-working Slurm/Kubernetes layer and no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 attestation; ClusterMAX 3.0 (23 Sep 2026) kept it there without re-testing: 'We need to verify that these operational problems are fixed'

Boosteroid (cloud gaming) holds a 2024 master agreement for 489 servers (~US$7.9M through Nov 2029) with an option the company values at up to ~US$700M over five years; DNA Fund's 1,192-GPU agreement was terminated in Nov 2025 with US$7.3M receivable
productsAndServices.positioning: The 10-K names CoreWeave, Crusoe Energy, Nebius and Lambda Labs as competitors and says the company targets 'small and medium-sized customers with high returns'. Against those peers it is small (US$68.8M of FY2025 cloud revenue), unrated below Bronze by SemiAnalysis, and repositioning 'toward longer-duration enterprise deployments, managed infrastructure services, and next-generation GPU capacity' (Q1 2026 release).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct reserved and managed contracts (12-month minimum for a 256-GPU reserved cluster); on-demand through the Shadeform marketplace (B200 from May 2025); customer-funded managed services
targetSegments: AI labs and inference platforms (BaseTen, Prime Intellect, Hyperbolic)
enterprises wanting managed private AI (HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001 alignment, air-gapped options)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Paris RFS 30 Sep 2026; BaseTen revenue from Nov 2026; Iceland B300 Dec 2026; Sydney capacity from Q4 2026; Prime Intellect Vera Rubin Q2 2027; Krambu 100 MW from 2027 (all company targets)

productsAndServices.name: Enovum data centres — colocation and build-to-suit leasing (the 'Colocation services' segment)
productsAndServices.description: Enovum Data Centers Corp., bought by Bit Digital in October 2024 for CAD 62.8M, develops Tier 3-design halls, mostly by retrofitting industrial buildings, and leases them under build-to-suit and modified-gross colocation agreements with pass-throughs. The 10-K says the 'average build time for retrofits is intended to be approximately six months' and the 'average build-out cost per MW (gross) is approximately $8 to $10 million, as compared to an industry average of approximately $13 million'. Sites: MTL-1 (3195 Chemin de Bedford, Montreal, 4 MW gross, leased to 2036, 14 to 15 customers, 3 MW IT, fully occupied); MTL-2 (7300 Trans-Canada Hwy, Pointe-Claire, 5 MW gross, owned since Dec 2024, development paused and then restarted in Q3 2026 for delivery 'near the end of the fiscal year'); MTL-3 (Saint-Jérôme, 7 MW gross / 5 MW IT, Cerebras as sole tenant on a five-year term billing CAD 1.4M a month from 1 Nov 2025, purchase option of CAD 24.2M closed May 2026); NC-1 (Madison, NC, see the specs table); and NC-2/NC-3 in Yadkin County, NC (US$60M agreement of 16 Aug 2026, closing Q4 2026).
highlights: Colocation revenue: US$1.4M (FY2024), US$8.9M (FY2025), US$4.8M (Q1 2026), US$4.7M (Q2 2026); remaining performance obligations of US$932.9M at 30 Jun 2026, almost all the Nscale contract

Nscale: 10-year, 40 MW IT colocation agreement at NC-1 signed 18 Dec 2025, 'approximately $865 million' of contracted revenue including escalators and installation, excluding electricity; two 20 MW phases with ready-for-service targets of 30 Apr and 30 May 2026; 'backed by an investment-grade hyperscaler offtake'; initial billing began in Q3 2026 with full run-rate billing on 40 MW expected in August 2026

Capacity roadmap (Sep 2026 deck, gross MW online): 11 MW at end-2025, about 65 MW in Q3 2026, about 70 MW at end-2026 and 175 MW at end-2027, against a 10-K target of 76 MW by Q4 2026; pipeline described as about 1.3 to 1.5 GW

NC-2/NC-3: two former Unifi buildings in Yadkinville (about 62 and 63 acres), 'a combined minimum of 60 MW of initial gross utility capacity' with 'potential to support up to approximately 200 MW', RFS Q3 2027, non-binding LOIs 'with investment-grade credit support'; Yadkin County adopted a two-year data-centre moratorium on 18 Aug 2026 that covers unincorporated areas only
productsAndServices.positioning: The 10-K names Digital Realty, Equinix, NTT, CyrusOne, STACK Infrastructure, Aligned and Iron Mountain as competitors. WhiteFiber's differentiation is the retrofit: former factories (a Unifi yarn plant at NC-1, a mattress factory at MTL-3) converted in months at a stated US$8 to 10 million per gross MW, sold to one or two tenants per site rather than to the multi-tenant market.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term build-to-suit and colocation leases (10 years for Nscale, 5 years for Cerebras) with electricity passed through; MTL-1 retail colocation on about 2.5-year average terms
targetSegments: enterprise and retail colocation in Montreal (MTL-1)
productsAndServices.roadmap: MTL-2 delivery near end-2026; NC-1 toward 99 gross MW by May 2029 and 'approximately 300 gross megawatts over time'; NC-2/NC-3 RFS Q3 2027; 'more than 100 MW of additional capacity online' in 2027 (21 Aug 2026 release)

productsAndServices.name: NC-1 development and site power — the owner's scope at Madison, North Carolina
productsAndServices.description: WhiteFiber, through Enovum NC-1 Bidco, LLC, owns the former Unifi Manufacturing plant at 805 Island Drive, Madison (about 1,000,000 sq ft, 96 acres per WFDD), bought for US$45M base cash on 20 May 2025 with earn-outs tied to Duke delivering 99 MW. It holds the Duke Energy Carolinas capacity letter of 16 May 2025 (24 MW gross 'on or about September 1, 2025', 40 MW 'on or about April 1, 2026', 99 MW 'within four (4) years'; 24 kV three-phase service; Duke 'does not guarantee timelines can be met') and Unifi's electric service agreement, assigned on 4 Aug 2025, under which Duke owns the substation, transformers, breakers and metering as 'Extra Facilities' for a US$11,405 monthly charge. WhiteFiber posted a US$3M surety bond to Duke in July 2026. Behind the meter it buys 'power distribution equipment, generators, and cooling systems' (10-K) and intends 'natural gas fuel cell generation technology' behind the meter 'by partnering with third-party energy providers'.
highlights: Duke 'has completed the work required to deliver the initial 54 gross MW of utility power to the site' (14 May 2026); about US$150M of equity invested by Dec 2025

The medium-voltage switchgear issue: disclosed 14 May 2026 as 'a recently identified supply-chain-related issue affecting certain medium-voltage switchgear components'; the Q1 call called it 'not a broad equipment availability issue' and moved delivery to a 'scaled ramp-up'; on the Q2 call (12 Aug 2026) the CEO said 'The pace of the ramp was affected by delivering and commissioning issues involving certain switchgear equipment. Those issues have since been resolved.' No supplier is named in any document

Long-term power: management 'believes' NC-1 'may receive and support up to 200 MW (gross)' subject to 'developing new substations', and the Q2 release speaks of 'approximately 300 gross megawatts over time'; the marketing page lists 98 MW by Q4 2027 and 298 MW by Q2 2028

Financing: a US$100M delayed-draw term loan from Bit Digital Capital, Inc. (20 May 2026; 9.5% plus a 1.1x MOIC; US$80M drawn by 31 Jul 2026; a US$20M tranche assigned to B. Riley Securities) bridges a proposed NC-1 project financing with 'a consortium of lenders' in exclusivity as of Aug 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Compared with the landlords in this corpus (Tract sells powered ground; PowerHouse and Prime build to suit), WhiteFiber is a retrofitter that converts an existing industrial connection: NC-1's first 54 gross MW came through Unifi's assigned service agreement rather than a new large-load interconnection.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Owner-developer; the tenant lease (Nscale) funds the build through project-level debt
productsAndServices.roadmap: 99 gross MW by May 2029 (Duke letter); 200 to 300 gross MW with new substations (management belief)

productsAndServices.name: WhiteFiber Continuum — cross-data-centre supercluster networking
productsAndServices.description: A dark-fibre interconnect that joins GPU clusters in separate buildings into one training domain. The Q2 2026 10-Q reports R&D results of '111.2 Tbps of bandwidth across 83 kilometers of dark fiber with a guaranteed round-trip latency of 0.9 milliseconds', patent applications filed and a commercial launch targeted for Q3 2026; the product page claims 136 Tbps, developed with Weka.
highlights: Announced 9 Jul 2026; commercial availability 'Q3 2026' per the product page; no customer named
productsAndServices.positioning: Aimed at the problem the company's own footprint creates: small halls (4 to 7 MW in Montreal) that need to be joined to host one large job.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with cloud and colocation contracts (company description)
targetSegments: training customers across multiple WhiteFiber sites

recentDevelopments.headline: Duke Energy Carolinas letter agreement: 24 MW, then 40 MW, then 99 MW 'within four (4) years'; 'Duke Energy does not guarantee timelines can be met'
recentDevelopments.read: The 99 MW that the market repeats is an efforts-based schedule from the utility.

relationships.note: Nscale is WhiteFiber's anchor tenant: a 10-year, 40 MW IT colocation agreement at NC-1 worth about US$865M, 'backed by an investment-grade hyperscaler offtake', which is 93% of WhiteFiber's remaining performance obligations.
relationships.context:
Signed 18 Dec 2025 by Enovum NC-1 Bidco, LLC. Two 20 MW phases were to be ready for service on 30 Apr and 30 May 2026; the dates moved to 31 May after 'customer requested certain design modifications', then into Q3 2026 after the medium-voltage switchgear issue. Initial billing began in Q3 2026 and the full 40 MW run rate was expected in August 2026 (Q2 call). WhiteFiber gives Nscale priority notification of further capacity.

Nscale's S-1 (18 Sep 2026) does not name WhiteFiber, Enovum or NC-1. It records a US$1.2B delayed-draw GPU term loan for 'the applicable data center' in North Carolina, arranged by Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan, rated investment grade, and maturing no later than 27 Dec 2031. The corpus's Nscale dossier records the Madison site as 'partner-run' with '99MW secured Duke Energy'; the Duke agreements are WhiteFiber's, not Nscale's.

relationships.scale: 54 gross MW delivered; 99 MW letter target by May 2029
relationships.via: Duke Energy Carolinas electric service at NC-1
relationships.note: Duke Energy Carolinas is NC-1's utility: a 16 May 2025 letter agreement with Enovum sets 24, 40 and 99 MW phases, and Unifi's electric service agreement was assigned to Enovum NC-1 Bidco on 4 Aug 2025.
relationships.context:
The letter, signed by Duke's Stu Heishman, states an estimated peak load of 99 MW at 24 kV, promises 'commercially reasonable efforts' on the three phases and says Duke 'does not guarantee timelines can be met'. Under the assigned service agreement Duke owns the 'Extra Facilities' (overhead lines, substations, transformers, breakers, metering) for a US$11,405 monthly charge. Duke completed the work for the initial 54 gross MW by May 2026, and WhiteFiber posted a US$3M surety bond in July 2026.

No Duke document names WhiteFiber, Enovum or Nscale; Duke's investor decks caption Microsoft, Amazon and QTS sites only. The relationship is recorded from WhiteFiber's filings and the Duke-countersigned letter it filed.

policyExposure.regime: North Carolina large-load tariff (Duke Energy Carolinas rate case)
policyExposure.exposure: NC-1 takes service from Duke Energy Carolinas under Unifi's assigned electric service agreement and NCUC-approved tariffs. Duke's 2026 North Carolina rate-case settlements route a large-load tariff to a separate expedited proceeding to finish before new rates take effect on 1 Jan 2027 (per the corpus's Duke dossier). WhiteFiber's 99 MW target and any expansion beyond it would fall under whatever minimum-bill and term rules that proceeding sets; the company's filings do not discuss it.

Yadkin County commissioners adopted a two-year moratorium on data-centre development in unincorporated areas on 18 Aug 2026, the day after WhiteFiber announced NC-2/NC-3. The Unifi properties sit inside Yadkinville's town limits, which the town manager says face 'no legal or zoning hurdle', and the county manager confirmed the moratorium 'only addresses the unincorporated areas of the county'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Enovum's Jon Collins told WFDD the company reuses existing buildings 'so an abandoned facility does not become a drag on the county'.

policyExposure.regime: North Carolina qualifying data-centre sales and use tax exemption
policyExposure.exposure: The IPO prospectus describes NC-1 as a qualified North Carolina data centre for the state's sales and use tax exemption on electricity and eligible equipment (per the 424B4).

The 10-K risk factors state that battery storage systems and cooling systems used in the North American data centres 'are manufactured in or pass through Mexico', exposing the build programme to tariff changes on that route; no specific rate or mitigation is given.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that WhiteFiber's value to a power-equipment seller is the landlord, not the cloud. Basis: US$932.9M of the US$1,008.0M remaining performance obligations at 30 Jun 2026 are colocation; B. Riley values NC-1 alone at US$1.56B against a US$719M market capitalisation; the cloud has been rated 'Underperforming' twice and lost its 70.7% customer. Indicator to watch: the NC-1 project financing closing (in exclusivity since August 2026) and the size of the NC-2/NC-3 leases 'during the fourth quarter of 2026'.

(High confidence) We assess that the company is the buyer of record for everything behind Duke's meter at NC-1, and that medium-voltage switchgear is the category where that authority has already been tested. Basis: the ESA leaves substations, transformers and breakers with Duke as 'Extra Facilities'; the 10-K lists power distribution equipment, generators and cooling as WhiteFiber's procurements; the 14 May 2026 disclosure and the Q2 call attribute the Nscale slip to 'certain medium-voltage switchgear components' and to 'delivering and commissioning issues involving certain switchgear equipment'. Collection gap: no supplier, general contractor or switchgear specification is named anywhere. Indicator to watch: NC-2/NC-3 long-lead orders in the Q3 2026 10-Q.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the 99 MW at NC-1 is a schedule, not a contract, and that the delivered 54 gross MW is the only firm figure. Basis: Duke's letter promises 'commercially reasonable efforts' and 'does not guarantee timelines'; the 10-K says no service agreement above 99 MW has been received; the 200 MW and 300 MW figures are management's belief and a marketing page. Indicator to watch: an executed Duke service agreement for the third phase, or the earn-out payments to Unifi that trigger only if Duke delivers or contracts 99 MW.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Bit Digital's control will persist but shrink by financing rather than by sale. Basis: Bit Digital pledged not to sell in 2026 and holds a fixed 27.04 million shares, yet its stake fell from about 70% to about 59.9% in one convertible exchange; the parent lends to NC-1 at 9.5% plus a 1.1x MOIC funded by Ethereum-collateralised borrowing at 5.45%. Indicator to watch: the 2027 expiry of the transition services agreement and any change in the shared CEO seat.

(Low confidence) We assess that on-site generation at WhiteFiber sites will be natural-gas fuel cells owned by a third party, and that batteries and SSTs are not in view. Basis: the 10-K's stated intent to deploy fuel-cell generation 'by partnering with third-party energy providers'; the only battery mention is a supply-chain risk factor; nothing on first-party channels mentions 800 VDC or solid-state transformers. This is an inference from stated intent, with no supplier, site or permit on the record. Indicator to watch: a named fuel-cell provider at NC-1 or NC-2/NC-3.

financials.commentary: A public filer since August 2025 with two segments and a fiscal year ending 31 December. The record's tension is between a US$1.0B contracted backlog and a company that has missed three of its first four EPS prints, burned its IPO proceeds inside a year and refinanced through two convertibles and a related-party loan. The Q3 2026 report is expected around mid-November 2026 (Q3 2025 was reported on 13 Nov 2025); no date has been announced.
